Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life · Travel & transport

pilgrimage noun

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.107 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. pilgrimage

peregrīnātiō, peregrīnātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

travel abroad; a pilgrimage

Classically a stay or a journey abroad; with religiōnis ergō or causā it is a pilgrimage. Egeria’s Itinerarium tells of one, to the Holy Land in the 380s.

Other words

  • peregrīnātiō religiōnis ergō

    also used · Renaissance · Erasmus, Colloquia, the title of a colloquy (loci-erasmus)

  • sacra peregrīnātiō

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. pilgrimage, after Egger

See also pilgrim, monastery.

SourcesLewis & Short: peregrinatio · Lewis & Short: religio

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. pilgrimage. Morgan–Owens prints ergā for Erasmus’s ergō.

The title of Erasmus’s colloquy as the Latinitas loci collection gives it (loci-erasmus).
